class_query_hits.found: rnams ooo ka re lhan du gsungs
class_query_hits.expected: rnams shlooo ka re lhan du gsungs
class_query_hits.evidence: The wylie conversion drops the ACIP Sanskrit brace code {SHl} (sh with subjoined la), leaving the orphan `ooo ka`, which cannot be a Tibetan syllable sequence - no consonant, and a tripled vowel letter. The acip field of this same row preserves the source: "SKYE BA KUN TU RNAMS {SHl}OOO KA RE LHAN DU GSUNGS,". Measured over the whole spine: 23 rows carry a {SHl} brace code and all 23 lose the `shl` in their wylie (count of rows where acip matches '%{SHl}OO%' and wylie matches '%oo ka%' but not '%shl%' = 23 of 23); by contrast 9 rows spell the word without the brace code as SHLOO KA and all 9 keep it, wylie `shloo ka` (e.g. TITLS:1252 acip "...POD SO SOR SHLOO KA RE" -> wylie "...pod so sor shloo ka re"; also C03:349 and C07:80). Two of the damaged rows are in this same document: C03:302 acip "LHA YI SKAD DANG SOGS {SHl}OO KA RE RE" -> wylie "lha yi skad dang sogs oo ka re re"; C03:378 acip "ZHES PA'I {SHl}OO KA GCIG STE" -> wylie "zhes pa'i oo ka gcig ste". The word is Sanskrit shloka, "verse", which is what the English of this segment renders ("the various verses"). `expected` above is the converter-faithful output for this row's source as keyed; the residual tripled vowel is a separate source defect, filed below, after which the reading is `shloo ka`. Effect: the word is unsearchable and unreadable in the wylie layer in all 23 rows.

class_query_hits.evidence: After a final -g the nominalizer takes the pa/par form, not ba/bar (standard 'jug pa, 'jug par). The sense here is unambiguously 'wishing to enter the door', so the alternative reading of bar as the separate noun 'interval / up to' is excluded. Spine check, span-level: exactly five segments contain the string 'jug bar, and I inspected all five — three (C03:367, C16:431, TCS11:199) are zung 'jug bar gyi, where bar IS the noun 'up to', and the remaining two are this sentence, duplicated verbatim at C16:412. So the nominalizer reading of bar after -g occurs nowhere else in the spine. The same orthographic rule holds elsewhere: all twelve thob bar segments are ma ... thob bar du ('until'), the noun again. By contrast 'jug par appears in 151 segments (a segment count, i.e. an upper bound on distinct spans, not a span-level tally). The ACIP column of this segment reads 'JUG BAR as well, so the deviation sits in the transcription source, not in spine ingest. Not an instance of any registered systematic class (no footnote fusion, folio marker, or glued-on heading). No span keys to the defect: bar is nulled on independent grounds.

class_query_hits.expected: zhes pa'i shloo ka gnyis kyis bstan te
class_query_hits.evidence: "oo ka" is not a word in Tibetan or Sanskrit; the sense required is shloka (verse) — "this is taught by these two verses". This segment's own ACIP reads ",ZHES PA'I {SHl}OO KA GNYIS KYIS BSTAN TE,": the braced Sanskrit-letter token {SHl} was dropped wholesale by the ACIP-to-Wylie converter. The defect tracks the BRACE NOTATION, not the reading — where the same word is keyed without braces the Wylie survives intact, verified in-spine at C03:349 (ACIP "ZHES PA'I SHLOO KA GCIG GIS BSTAN," -> Wylie "zhes pa'i shloo ka gcig gis bstan"), C07:80 (ACIP ",ZHES PA'I SHLOO KA GCIG STE," -> Wylie "zhes pa'i shloo ka gcig ste"), and TITLS:847, 1252, 1282, 1289, 2514, 2570. Measured over the whole spine by this reconciler: 23 segments carry {SHl} in ACIP; 0 of the 23 retain "shl" anywhere in Wylie; exactly 22 segments have a bare " oo ka" in Wylie and all 22 are {SHl}OO KA segments; the 23rd is C03:300, whose ACIP "{SHl}OOO KA" became Wylie "ooo ka" — a complete 23/23 correspondence, so this is a systematic converter defect, not a local corruption. The 23 are C03:300, 302, 378, 403, 432, 463, 478, 495, 505, 515, 524, 546, 560, 574 and C16:414, 450, 463, 479, 482, 484, 492, 499, 507. PARALLEL-WITNESS CHECK PERFORMED: C16:450 carries the identical "zhes pa'i oo ka gnyis kyis bstan te", but its ACIP is also "{SHl}OO KA", so it is the same artefact propagated through the same converter, not an independent published reading. Consequence: the citation-count colophon does not match the dictionary and "oo ka" is unsearchable as a word.

class_query_hits.found: nyes dmigs ri gnas thar pa'i bde ba la

class_query_hits.evidence: Misplaced syllable boundary in the ACIP of record (C03:432 reads 'NYES DMIGS RI GNAS'): 'ri gnas' (mountain abode) is not a possible reading after 'nyes dmigs', while 'rig nas' (having realized) is what the syntax requires and what GMR translates ('Bless me to perceive'). Parallel witnesses checked in the spine: C16:463 carries the identical string 'ri gnas', but it is the same ACI course transcription of this verse, so it is a shared inheritance rather than an independent witness. The independent witness is the root text, TCS08SourceOfAllMyGood:6, whose wylie reads 'nyes dmigs rig nas thar pa'i bde ba la', whose ACIP reads 'NYES DMIGS RIG NAS', and whose phonetic line reads 'nyemik rikne tarpay dewa la' (rikne = rig nas). 'rig nas' is also the form C03 itself uses elsewhere (C03:153 'rig nas dang po'i gnyen por', C03:459 'mthong zhing rig nas'); 'ri gnas' occurs nowhere in the spine except these two course segments. Not filed: the same TCS08 line reads 'don gnyer chen por skye bar' against 'chen po skye bar' here; that is a legitimate grammatical variant. The 'oo ka' for '{SHl}OO KA' is the registered converter-drop class and is not re-filed.

class_query_hits.found: THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I GO 'PANG BSGRUB PA
class_query_hits.expected: THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I GO 'PHANG BSGRUB PA
class_query_hits.evidence: Confirmed from this segment's own text. ACIP (source of record) reads GO 'PANG; the wylie field carries the same reading, go 'pang, so this is in the source, not the converter. The word is go 'phang (rank, station, state), which is what GMR translates: 'the state of All-Knowing'. Re-derived corpus counts: acip LIKE '%GO ''PANG%' returns exactly one row, C03:445; acip LIKE '%GO ''PHANG%' returns 219; the wylie field splits identically, 1 vs 219. Stronger still, the syllable 'pang occurs NOWHERE else in the corpus wylie: a-chung ('a) prefixes only voiced or aspirated radicals in Tibetan orthography ('g 'j 'd 'b 'dz 'kh 'ch 'th 'ph 'tsh), so 'p- is not a spellable syllable onset and 'pang cannot be a variant. Parallel-witness check: no other segment carries this passage (english LIKE '%habit of hoping for the%', english LIKE '%up to the final end%', wylie LIKE '%tshe ''di snang gi zhen pa%', wylie LIKE '%rang res ngan ''gro%' each return C03:445 alone). The exact collocation mkhyen pa'i go 'p… appears in seven other rows, every one of them 'phang: C01:84, C16:32, TCS02:315, TCS09:37, Sunlight:595, Sunlight:707, SPF:461. The nearest relative for the surrounding idiom, ILL:126 (thog mtha' bar gsum du gal che), shares only that closing idiom and says nothing about go 'phang. Registered classes checked and not applicable: no {SHl} drop, no fused footnote number, no folio marker, no glued heading; the ACIP trailing shad ',' absent from the wylie is the normal strip, and ACIP TSE for wylie tshe is the ACIP convention (TS = tsh), not an error. A dropped aspiration H in one row against 219 correct ones, yielding an impossible syllable, is a keystroke error.
